A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Stable Flow and contain complete main texts and supplementary material. Their equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-editing experiments, quantitative baseline comparisons, ablations, and a human preference study, including supplementary FLUX and SD3 results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds a vision-language-model evaluation of editing results in Appendix B.3 and Table 5.

M1.justification: Vital-layer identification, selective attention injection, latent nudging, and latent caching remain unchanged. The new Figure 11 specifies the source keys and values used during injection, clarifying the existing procedure without establishing a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the COCO-derived editing benchmark, generated-image examples, and FLUX and SD3 demonstrations. The new VLM evaluation introduces no reported new dataset, domain, or editing task.

E2.justification: SDEdit, P2P+NTI, Instruct-P2P, MagicBrush, and MasaCTRL remain the evaluated baselines. New Table 5 evaluates the same five methods. Its inconsistent citation numbers do not establish different comparators; the method names and accompanying discussion identify them.

E3.justification: Appendix B.3 adds Phi-3.5-vision evaluation using binary judgments of text following and modification of only essential image parts. Existing CLIP metrics, dataset filtering, generation settings, and human-study procedures are retained. The new evaluation's sample count is unspecified.

E4.justification: The layer-count sensitivity analysis is corrected: v1 Appendix B.3/Figure 22 reports negligible changes after removing 80% of vital layers; v2 Appendix B.4/Figure 23 says 20%. The tested fractions and displayed examples are unchanged, as are the other ablations.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix A.1 newly reports per-layer perceptual-similarity variances. This adds dispersion reporting without documenting additional runs. The user-study rating counts and binomial significance tests remain unchanged.

E6.justification: New Table 5 reports Stable Flow at 83.33% text following and 61.66% essential-only modification, versus MagicBrush at 88.33% and 46.66%. These are additional evaluation results, not same-setting performance gains over v1. Tables 1–4 remain unchanged; the layer-removal finding changes from 80% to 20%.

T1.justification: The vitality definition, vital-layer threshold, flow formulation, Euler equations, and approximation assumption remain mathematically equivalent. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: automatic vital-layer identification, training-free editing through selective injection, and improved real-image inversion through latent nudging.

C2.justification: v2 narrows the stated tolerance to removing vital layers and interprets the new VLM results as corroborating the CLIP-based preservation/adherence tradeoff. The limitations concerning style changes, object dragging, and complete background replacement remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Figure 11 newly specifies that edited-image queries are retained while source-image keys and values are injected. Appendix B.3 documents the VLM evaluator and its two questions. Existing implementation links, layer sets, sampling settings, and nudging details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to the Phi-3 technical report, Fast Imagic, and Forgedit. It removes the Add-it reference and the paragraph contrasting that concurrent object-insertion method with Stable Flow. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes local wording and notation edits, expands Appendix A.1, inserts the VLM-evaluation subsection, and moves acknowledgments before the references. The main narrative and section organization receive limited revision.

P2.justification: v2 adds the attention-injection schematic and VLM results table, relocates Figure 2, and rearranges supplementary displays, including the SD3 plot. Existing layer-bypassing grids are downsampled, and the layer-count caption is corrected. Existing visual results are retained.

improvement.justification: The attention diagram, variance reporting, and correction of the misleading 80%-removal statement improve clarity and accuracy. The VLM evaluation adds limited corroboration, although its sample count is unspecified. Removal of relevant Add-it context and incorrect citation numbers in Table 5 temper these gains, but the overall revision provides a modest improvement.
